limitations: Population media are rendered from the population's own (MIND) text: images are poster cards, audio is flite speech after a synthesized jingle, video is narrated slides with subtitles (D-33); no photographs, music performances or filmed video (no such corpus exists under /workspace/data/crucible).

content_open@1 inputs own_creator_views, own_item_exposures and own_item_consumed are 0/1 flags from exact audience sets (counts are not kept); own_topic is the in-world analogue of KuaiRand's user_tag_lift > 0 (D-34). The random-exposure experiment and the fitted open decision reach civilisations only once civ uses social.worlds.feed_config.

Engagement integrity: colluders who do not follow each other and each have a footprint are indistinguishable from independent fans by state; a genuine 3+ friend group with no outside attention is excluded (D-35).

Social-to-economy chains depend on economy.work's own shop rules (a shop session considers only steps nobody serves for the member: a social lead cannot make a member switch from a poor provider). Recommendations: a member still relying on a service after 3 uses (>= 1 accepted; work cancels a provider whose own valuation turned negative) writes about it with a hand-set p 0.35 per creation; a reader with that task looks into it (a shop session 30 min later) with hand-set p 0.9 / 0.6 / 0.2 by what it uses now. Not fitted. The chain metric reads causal order in the log; the shop finds the product through search, so a chain does not prove the post caused the adoption.

SP-4.5b's primary outcome (competing feed slots in the first session after a randomised inbox placement) follows from finite slots almost by construction; views and seconds of competing content are reported as secondary outcomes.

Behaviour models of the population on the social platforms (creation, messaging, subscriptions, communities, product discovery) are hand-set and unvalidated (FIDELITY_REGISTER rows); only content_open@1 on shorts is fitted.

Relationship and community kinds keep copies outside this package: pop.contacts / pop.communities (B), forum.forum_follows / forum_boards (4.0 forum); in crowd-stand-in worlds aud still keeps follower sets. SP-2.3 shared_primitive_kinds is not raised to 19 by C alone (forum, population and F migrations are other owners' files; integration notes).

Creator memberships (social.creators) still bill with their own bank.move of ledger kind subscription, not through commerce subs (F+G integration note: MRR/churn metrics of subs do not see them). Not changed this wave: products/subs offer no membership delivery type, and the change spans commerce.

Population governance of communities (wave 3b continuation, social.popsocial._govern): stewards appoint moderators, propose pruning and member votes, members vote; hand-set, no factions or strategic voting; tested by a unit test, not yet measured at 40-day scale (SP-4.7b reports it).

The social browser pages are reachable only through social.web.make_social_web_app; the deployable entry point (crucible.web.app.main -> make_web_app) does not register them (audit C skeptic S6; web/ is not this package: integration note).

Measurement on this branch is unofficial (snapshot runs in shared slots) and partly pending: the four failures found on 2026-11-27 (C.3 provenance, D.3, SP-4.6b, SP-4.8b) are fixed with regression tests but their gate re-runs were still queued when this agent finished; SP-4.7b was running.

Audience value (MASTER_SPEC 4.4, audit C skeptic S7): a viewer's satisfaction gain is fraction read x (affinity - reference), so a fully read blurb is worth as much as a fully read substantial piece; information received (e.g. seconds of non-redundant content read, redundancy from the bytes' compressibility) is not modelled. Changing it shifts every consumption-driven gate and needs a calibration pass; not done this wave.

ECON: members who rely on a service that works for them write recommendation posts naming its address; viewers with that task in their work look into it (a shop session 30 min later, social.popinbox._service_leads) with a probability set by what they use for that task now (lead_probability). A 'social' candidate channel in economy.work._candidates (items the individual viewed that name a host) would make discovery through content explicit instead of going through search. Also: work.act_shop considers only unserved steps (_wants_help), so a social lead reaching a member who relies on a poor provider cannot lead to switching; considering underserved steps (relied on, low own belief) would let recommendations change who serves whom (MASTER_SPEC 4.8). A lead check on this branch (startup world, one post naming a host read by 40 members with that need): 33 leads -> 21 considered the named product (via search) -> 17 adopted it.
